title: Refuse readings whose criteria rest on the producer's report
summary: Root cause: nothing compares a criterion's required evidence with what the verifier can observe, so criteria like "the report lists the Grep" (jobs gk9e, vrsk, yckz and two others) are accepted and then cannot be judged. Add a mechanism check in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs, run next to check_prior_result_and_scope when a reading is built, that refuses any criterion citing the producer's report, summary, claims or statement as its evidence. The error names the criterion and says to restate it as a command or Grep the verifier can run, or a file in the snapshot. Audience: Athena's operator and the verifier.

defaults_applied.how: The rule is enforced by a code check, not prose in a prompt.
New unit tests; fmt, clippy and test must pass.
Fix at reading acceptance, covering every criterion, not one job's wording.
Criteria run tests that show refusal and acceptance behavior.
Check is written in Rust in athena-core.
One focused check plus tests and a changelog entry.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The cause originates at reading acceptance, where criteria are first fixed; the code check is the mechanism, matching what all five introspections proposed.
The reader prompt has 3 tokens of headroom, so no prompt text is added; the refusal message teaches the reader on retry.
The refusal is reported the same way as check_prior_result_and_scope (a reading-refused message), applied to every reading with a capability, not only retries.

The named jobs 20261027-004517-gk9e and 20261027-011733-vrsk are cited as evidence of the failure class, not retried here; their earlier findings (unobservable report criterion) are the class this change prevents, and the gh transport move itself already landed in 20261027-012938-yckz.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test --locked -p athena-core reading`: a new test shows a reading with the criterion "the producer's report lists the caller-check Grep" is refused with an error naming that criterion, and the same test fails when the new check is removed.

Run `cargo test --locked -p athena-core reading`: a test covers each phrase family ("the report lists", "the producer states", "the producer confirms", "producer's summary", "producer's claims") and each is refused.

Run `cargo test --locked -p athena-core reading`: a test shows criteria naming a command, a Grep, or a file path (e.g. "a Grep of crates/ for `gh::` outside gh/ returns no hits", "cargo test --locked passes") are accepted, so ordinary readings are not refused.

Run `cargo test --locked -p athena-core reading`: a test shows the check is wired into the reading path (the reader's output becomes a refusal message, not a Reading) for a first attempt as well as a retry, not only in the check function.

The doc comment on the new check and the CHANGELOG.md entry name the root cause: criteria were written without a defined list of what the verifier can observe, and nothing compared required evidence with that list; jobs 20261027-004517-gk9e, 20261027-011733-vrsk, 20261027-012938-yckz, 20261026-232402-6qme and 20261026-232423-hvyb are cited.
Run `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked`; all pass.

out_of_scope: Editing prompt files (reader has 3 tokens of headroom)
Changing the verifier's handover or giving the verifier the producer's report
Changes to athena.toml, defaults.toml or workflows
Reverting or redoing the gh transport move
urgent_reason: Cuts rejected and failed attempts: five jobs were rejected or failed because a criterion needed the producer's report, which the verifier never sees.
hard_reason: Changes the gate that judges readings for all other jobs, so a mistaken pattern could wrongly refuse valid readings.
